description: blend/fillet-into-a-step's L with the step's face leaning, from (0, 1) to (lean, 2) in the xz plane — back over the tall block at lean −0.4, overhanging the low block in the variant at 0.3 — the low block's top front edge filleted at r 0.3. The face across is oblique to the edge, its arc an ellipse, and the tall block's front edge is slanted: the trim lies on that edge's line continued below the vertex, in the front cap, and the edge is lengthened along it (ADR-0038). Leaning back, the end plane lies over the low block and the blend stops short of x = 0; overhanging, it lies over the tall block and the blend cuts into it. The volume is the L less the blend's section swept between the end plane and x = 2; the area the L's, less the two contacts' strips, plus the blend's cylinder between its end arcs, the far end's spandrel moved to the step's face at sqrt(1 + lean²) its size. Open CASCADE builds the end with exact conics but places it off them: its volume is 2.4e-9 (default) and 1.6e-9 (overhang) relative from the closed form, its area 5.9e-9 and 4.2e-9, the same under its fixed-order, adaptive and Gauss–Kronrod integrations, and the error turns sign with the lean; Arris matches both closed forms to 1e-11. That is under ADR-0015's 1e-6, so the fixture's volume and area tolerances are 1e-8, not a claim the oracle is wrong

analytic.counts_differ: Open CASCADE keeps the consumed corner vertex on the lengthened corner edge, two edges of one line between the same two faces; Arris lengthens the one edge to the trim (ADR-0038)
